bad_lesson.question: how do i fix the off by one in binary search? show it with the three, seven, nine example
bad_lesson.spokenAnswer: take the list three, seven, nine. its length is three, but its last real index is two. high starts at len(nums), which is three, so when low climbs to three the loop still runs and reads nums[3], a slot that does not exist, and it crashes. the fix is to start high at len(nums) minus one, the last real index. now when low passes high the loop simply stops and returns not found.
